column1: # ZAP scan rule overrides — false positives / informational noise for a Next.js / Stellar app.
# Format: <rule-id>\t<action>\t<parameter>\t<evidence>\t<url>
# Actions:
#   IGNORE    — suppress the alert (false positive or intentional)
#   WARN      — downgrade to warning (still reported, does not fail the scan)
#   FAIL      — treat as failure (stricter than the ZAP default)
# Rule IDs are from the ZAP passive and active scanner rule sets.
# See https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/ for the full list.
# 10038 — Content Security Policy (CSP) header not set
#   Next.js sets CSP via next.config.mjs headers; ZAP sometimes misses it.
# 10063 — Permissions Policy header not set
#   Managed in next.config.mjs
# 10096 — Timestamp disclosure (server header)
#   Next.js development mode exposes timestamps in headers; not applicable in prod.
# 10021 — X-Content-Type-Options header missing
#   Next.js adds this automatically; ZAP can flag preflight OPTIONS responses.
# 40012 — Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
#   Stellar public keys (56-char base58) trigger some XSS pattern heuristics.
#   We sanitize all inputs via withSanitizedBody middleware; flag as warn only.
# 40014 — Cross Site Scripting (Persistent)
# ─── JWT / session token in URL false positives ──────────────────────────────
# 10024 — Information disclosure — sensitive information in URL
#   Invite links legitimately contain a JWT token query param (?token=…).
#   This is by design (single-use, short-lived) — suppress URL disclosure alert.
# 90022 — Application error disclosure
#   Our /api/health and /api/docs endpoints intentionally return structured JSON;
#   ZAP may flag JSON error envelopes as error disclosure.
# 10094 — Base64 disclosure
#   USDC amounts and Stellar transaction XDR are legitimately base64-encoded.
# 10049 — Storable and cacheable content
#   Static Next.js assets are intentionally cached with long TTLs.
# ─── Active scan rules to downgrade (not fail CI) ─────────────────────────────
# 40018 — SQL injection
#   We use parameterized queries everywhere; any finding here is worth a WARN
#   (investigate manually) rather than a hard CI failure.
# 40019 — SQL injection (MySQL specific)
# 40020 — SQL injection (Hypersonic specific)
# 40021 — SQL injection (Oracle specific)
# 40022 — SQL injection (PostgreSQL specific)
# 40024 — SQL injection (SQLite specific)
# 10055 — CSP scanner
#   Staging environment may have relaxed CSP; warn but don't fail.
# 10035 — Strict-Transport-Security header not set
#   Staging may not have HTTPS configured; warn only.
